briefdescription.para: The number of direct child test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Incremented for each call to test(), which creates a child test_case and runs it immediately. The child test cases are not kept after they run, so that the memory does not grow with the number of test cases; only their number is needed later, for the TAP plan.

briefdescription.para: The node name.

detaileddescription.para: Not owned; it points to a string whose lifetime exceeds that of the node. Derived classes may access this member directly, in addition to the public name() getter.

briefdescription.para: The next suite in the list of suites.

detaileddescription.para: Null for the last suite, and for the suites not in the list. Set by link() and unlink(), and read by the runner, which is a friend.

briefdescription.para: The test index, counting from 1.

detaileddescription.para: The position of this object within its parent, displayed by the TAP reporter in the ok/not ok lines. Set directly by the runner, which numbers the suites when it runs them, and by the top suite, which is always the first one.

briefdescription.para: A copy of the suite name.

detaileddescription.para: The suites registered with runner::add_suite(), and the static suites, run later, when the string passed to the constructor may no longer exist; the name is therefore copied here, and the name of the node points to this copy. The test cases, which run immediately, do not copy their names.

briefdescription.para: Reference to the test runner that owns this object.

detaileddescription.para: Provides access to the reporter, to the filter, and to the state of the session (the running test case, and the abort and listing flags), and is used when aborting.

briefdescription.para: Stopwatch of this suite.

detaileddescription.para: Measures the duration of the suite; started and stopped by run() (by the runner, for the top suite), and read by the reporters, which are friends.

briefdescription.para: The number of the most recent child test point.

detaileddescription.para: Test points are numbered from 1; the value is 0 before the first one. This number counts the checks and the nested test cases of this object, in execution order, as required by the TAP ok/not ok lines. It is incremented for each check (by the check result) and for each nested test case created.

briefdescription.para: Totals for the node.

detaileddescription.para: For the suites, the totals include the checks of all their test cases; for a test case, they include only its own checks, plus the counts of its direct nested test cases.

The check counters are updated by the check result, which is a friend; the test case counters by after_test_case_create(), when a nested test case ends. For a suite, the totals of each of its test cases are also added, by the same function.

briefdescription.para: The first suite in the list of suites.

detaileddescription.para: The list includes the registered and the static suites of all runners, sorted by name; each runner selects its own. The pointer is constant-initialised (constinit, in src/test.cpp), so it is null before any constructor runs, whatever the order of the static initialisation across translation units.
Constant-initialised, so it is null before any static constructor runs; the static suites constructed before the runner are therefore not lost.

briefdescription.para: Constructs a suite with a name, runner, and callable body.

detaileddescription.para: Protected, since the suite must be registered with the runner, which only runner::add_suite() and the static_suite constructor do.

Callable_T
The type of the callable object.
Args_T
The types of any additional callable arguments.
name
The suite name or description, used in reports; it is copied, so the string need not outlive the call.
test_runner
The test runner managing this suite.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked when the suite executes. Its first parameter must be suite&.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments forwarded to the callable after the leading suite& reference.
Stores the callable, binding its arguments, if any. The own index is initially 0; the runner assigns the final index before running the suite.

The name is copied into owned_name_, and the node name points to the copy, since the suite may run after the string passed by the caller was destroyed; the base is constructed with an empty name, since the copy does not exist yet. The copy is null-terminated, also when the view passed by the caller is not.

briefdescription.para: Counts a newly constructed child test case and executes it immediately.

detaileddescription.para: The child test case is a local object of create_test_case(), and is destroyed when that function returns.

test_case
The newly created test_case.
suite
The parent suite to which execution results are reported.
Returns
Nothing.
Counts test_case, which is a local object of the calling create_test_case(), and immediately invokes test_case::run() on it. The test case is not kept; only child_test_cases_count_ is needed later, for the TAP plan.

If the filter patterns do not select the test case (its own name at its nesting level, or the name of suite at level 0, which matters only for the top suite, since the other suites run only when selected), its body is not called: the reporter is notified with skip_test_case() and the parent's skipped test cases counter is incremented. The test case keeps its index and its place among the children, so the TAP plan of the parent remains complete.

Otherwise, while the test case runs, the runner keeps it as its innermost running test case (see suite::test()). The parent's executed test cases counter is incremented after the run, and, if the child failed (a failed check, or a failed nested test case), its failed test cases counter too, so that the parent fails as well, as in node-tap. The child's check counters are intentionally not merged into the parent totals; each test case reports only its own counters. The child's totals are, however, accumulated into suite so that the suite summary reflects all checks performed by its test cases.
While the test cases are listed (see runner_options::list_tests), the selected test case is listed by the runner, and neither run nor counted, except in child_test_cases_count_.
After the test execution was aborted (possible only when the abort handler threw an exception, which the application caught), the report is complete, so the test case is neither run nor reported.

memberdef.name: create_test_case

briefdescription.para: Creates a child test case, and runs it.

detaileddescription.para: The common body of suite::test() and test_case::test(), which differ only in the parent suite and the nesting depth of the test cases they create.
Always inlined into them, even without optimisations, since each nested test case adds one call chain to the stack, and a separate frame for this function would make it longer.

Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test case name or description, used in reports, and the location of the call to test().
parent_suite
The suite to which the test case belongs.
nesting_depth
The depth of nesting of the test case; 1 for the direct children of a suite.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
Binds the callable and its arguments into a local body, constructs the child test_case as a local object that refers to the body, with the next test point number of this node as its index, then passes it to after_test_case_create(), which counts and runs it.

The child test case and its body, with the copies of the arguments, are destroyed when this function returns, so the memory used by a test session does not grow with the number of test cases; the stack holds one test case and one body for each level of nesting being run. Since the body is not stored in a std::function, it is never allocated, whatever the size of the lambda captures and of the arguments.

briefdescription.para: Reports an exception that escaped the suite body as a failed check of the suite.

detaileddescription.para: The suite body may throw outside its test cases, for example in a set-up step; the test cases catch their own exceptions. The failure is reported without a source location, since the suites do not record one, and the location of the throw is not known.

what
The explanatory string of a std::exception, or nullptr for an exception of another type.
Returns
Nothing.
The failure is reported as a check of the suite: the test point number is incremented first, so that the TAP output numbers it after the test cases already run, and counts it in the plan of the suite, and the failed checks counter is incremented, so that the suite, and through it the session, fail.

The message is unexpected exception in the suite body: followed by what, or unexpected exception of unknown type in the suite body when what is nullptr; as for the test cases, the type of a std::exception is not shown.

detaileddescription.para: Called by runner::register_suite() and by the static_suite constructor, after the name was copied. The suite is inserted after the suites with names less than or equal to its own, so the list remains sorted by name, and the suites with the same name remain in the order of their insertion. The top suite is not inserted, since the runner runs it separately.

Parameters

Returns

Inserts the suite after the suites with names less than or equal to its own, so the list remains sorted by name, and the suites with the same name remain in the order of their insertion. No memory is allocated. This is the only place where the names of the suites are compared; the runners run the suites in the order of the list.

briefdescription.para: Adds a test case to the suite, and runs it.

detaileddescription.para:
Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test case name or description, used in reports; a string literal, a const char*, or a std::string, converted implicitly to test_case_name, which also captures the location of the call; it must remain valid while the test case runs.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
The test function template creates a test case (a test_case with nesting depth 1) and runs it immediately. It accepts a descriptive name, a callable object (such as a lambda or function pointer), and an optional list of arguments to be passed to the callable, after the leading test_case& reference. The test case is reported using the provided name.

The test case is created and run by create_test_case(), as a local object destroyed when it returns, together with its stored body and bound arguments; only the number of test cases is kept, for the TAP plan.

Each test case typically involves evaluating logical expressions, such as comparing a computed result to an expected value, with expect() or require(). When exceptions are enabled, it is also possible to verify whether evaluating an expression throws exceptions. Each check either passes or fails, and the suite totals count the passed and failed checks.

It is typically invoked within the body of a suite. When invoked from the body of a running test case (for example via a captured suite reference), the new test case could not be reported as a sibling of the running one, which has not ended; it is therefore created by the innermost running test case, with test_case::test(), and runs nested in it, as if test() had been called on that test case.

T
The type of the values.
Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
name
The common name of the test cases.

callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked with the test case and each value.
Returns

5.1.0
The list is iterated as a range.

briefdescription.para: Adds a test case to the suite for each value of a range or a tuple, and runs them.

detaileddescription.para: For each value, in order, a test case is added and run, as by test(), with the value as the argument of the callable, which is called as callable (test_case, value). The values may be a range (a container, an array, a span, or a view), or a tuple, whose values may have different types, for a generic callable:

Each test case is named after the common name, followed by the value in parentheses, written as in the messages of the checks (Sizes (16)); a value that cannot be written (see extension::printable), such as an application type without an operator<<, is replaced by its position, starting at 1 (Records (#2)). The location of all the test cases is that of the call.

Values_T
The type of the range or tuple of values.
Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
name
The common name of the test cases; a string literal, a const char*, or a std::string, converted implicitly to test_case_name, which also captures the location of the call.
values
The range or tuple of values.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked with the test case and each value.
Returns
Nothing.
5.1.0
Forwards to detail::test_each_value(), which adds the test cases with test(), so they are nested in the running test case, if any.

briefdescription.para: Aborts test execution via the owning runner, for a failed requirement.

detaileddescription.para: Private, since it is used only by the check result, a friend, for a failed requirement without exceptions; the user code calls runner::abort().

sl
The source location from which the abort is triggered.
Returns
Does not return.
Delegates to the private runner::abort(), as caused by a failed requirement, passing the supplied source location, so that the report identifies it. The runner then calls the abort handler, if any, and terminates the process via ::abort().

briefdescription.para: Executes the suite body by invoking the stored callable.

detaileddescription.para: Private, since the suites are run only once, by the runner, which is a friend.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Invokes the stored callable with this suite, surrounded by reporter calls to begin and end the suite.

When exceptions are enabled, an exception that escapes the callable, which can be thrown only outside the test cases, since they catch their own exceptions, is caught and reported as a failed check of this suite, and the suite ends normally, so that the run continues with the next suite; the test cases run before the exception remain reported, and the following ones are not run. A body declared noexcept cannot pass the exception on; the program is then terminated before it reaches this function.
As for the test cases, an exception thrown by the abort handler is passed on, without reporting it, and without ending the suite.

briefdescription.para: A named, runnable test suite registered with the test runner.

detaileddescription.para: suite represents a top-level named group of related test cases within the µTest++ framework. It is created by calling runner::add_suite(), which constructs the object and stores it in the runner's collection; the stored suites are run later by runner::run(), together with the static suites, sorted by name. Each suite records its own timing information and propagates its results to the owning runner.

The suites to be run, registered or static, are kept in a single list, sorted by name, which does not depend on the runner object: its head is a constinit pointer, initialised before any constructor runs, and the links are members of the suites. The list includes the suites of all runners; each runner runs those that refer to it, in the order of the list.

The body of a suite is supplied as a callable (typically a lambda) that receives a suite& reference as its first argument. Inside the body, suite::test() is called to create and run individual test cases.

The constructor is protected, since a suite constructed elsewhere would not be registered with the runner; the suites are created only by runner::add_suite(), by the derived static_suite, which registers itself, and by the runner, for its top_suite.
The class is non-copyable and non-movable to preserve unique ownership and consistent state throughout the test session.
